title: Yara and the Salt
premise: Orsen Kavanagh, a beast-speaker who has hidden their forbidden gift for twenty years among the charm-sellers of Greyharbor, is betrayed by a customer's confession and becomes prey in the crown's new magic hunt. Fleeing with Yara, a salt-witch exile and the last keeper of an old covenant between humans and dragons, Orsen discovers their gift is not a curse but a birthright: they are heir to the covenant's broken voice. As dragon-fire gutters toward extinction, the pair must gather scattered oath-keepers across three realms while the crown's hunter — Orsen's own estranged brother — closes in. In the end, Orsen chooses to speak the covenant aloud at the cost of their anonymity, reforging the bond between realms and finding a found family that finally makes their gift a home rather than a hiding place.
about_author: Lior Hartwell is the pen name of a former tide-pool naturalist who spent a decade writing field notes before turning to fantasy. They live on a windswept coast where they claim the gulls gossip back.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller's Stall
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A day in Greyharbor market: small charms, careful lies, and a whispered conversation with a stray dog that nearly exposes them. Introduces Yara, who buys a protection ward she doesn't seem to need. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as routine; the ache of a gift that must stay silent.

chapters.title: Proclamation at the Tide Gate
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The crown posts its edict: all gifted persons must surrender for 'covenant audit.' The market empties of warmth as neighbors eye each other. Yara returns to Orsen's stall after dark and reveals she knew about the dog. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into wary alliance.

chapters.title: Salt in the Wound
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She explains her exile from the salt-witch covens and shows Orsen a dying ember of dragon-fire kept in a salt jar — proof the covenant between realms is failing. She asks Orsen to help find the oath-keepers. Emotional beat: reluctant hope meeting old grief.

chapters.title: The Confession
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A desperate customer, caught by the hunters, trades Orsen's name for mercy. Hunters ransack the stall; Orsen escapes through the sewers with nothing but the clothes they wear and Yara waiting at the tide gate. Emotional beat: betrayal, and the strange freedom of having nothing left to hide behind.

chapters.title: Outlaw Road
chapters.summary: Orsen and Yara travel north through marsh country, hunted. Orsen speaks with animals for the first time without shame, learning the marsh herons saw riders ahead. First real use of the gift as a tool, not a secret. Emotional beat: tentative trust becoming partnership.

chapters.title: The Hunter with My Brother's Face
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, flashback braided with present pursuit. Crown hunter Tammas Kavanagh — Orsen's brother, who reported their childhood gift years ago — interrogates a village. Orsen watches from cover, unseen. Emotional beat: the wound of family that chose the law over blood.

chapters.title: Oath-Keeper of the Ash Orchard
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The pair finds the first oath-keeper: Maren, an ancient orchard-tender whose trees grow only where dragons once wept. Maren tests them, then gives Yara a shard of covenant-stone. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed as burden, not treasure.

chapters.title: What the Covenant Was
chapters.summary: Maren's tale, framed in Orsen's POV. Long ago dragons lent their fire to human hearths in exchange for being remembered; when humans forgot, the fire began to die. Orsen realizes their beast-speech is the covenant's voice, inherited. Emotional beat: awe curdling into terror of responsibility.

chapters.title: Riders on the Salt Flats
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Ambush on the flats; Yara uses forbidden salt-magic to blind the hunters, breaking her exile-oath further. They escape but Maren's orchard burns as retribution. Emotional beat: guilt, and the cost of choosing each other.

chapters.title: The Grieving Dragon
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Guided by covenant-stone, they reach a cave where the last waking dragon, Vessith, lies half-guttered like a banked coal. Orsen speaks with her — truly speaks — and learns what it costs a dragon to be forgotten. Emotional beat: communion; identity no longer something to hide.

chapters.title: Vessith's Bargain
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Vessith will lend her last flame to reforge the covenant only if the oath-keepers gather and speak the old words before midwinter. But one word can only be spoken by a Kavanagh — the family that helped break the covenant generations ago. Emotional beat: dread of destiny.

chapters.title: City of Ledgers
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. To find the remaining oath-keepers' names, they infiltrate the capital's archive, where Tammas now serves. Orsen, disguised, reads their own family's shame in the records. Emotional beat: grief reframed — understanding the brother who turned them in.

chapters.title: A Brother's Ledger
chapters.summary: Tammas's POV. He has suspected the charm seller was his sibling since the edict posted. Torn between duty and memory, he falsifies one report — and damns himself. Emotional beat: love expressed as treason against his own conscience.

chapters.title: The Drowned Chapel
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Second oath-keeper found: Brother Ilex, a monk keeping vigil in a flooded chapel, guarding the spoken words of the covenant. He agrees to come, but warns the final speaking may kill the speaker. Emotional beat: sacrifice named plainly for the first time.

chapters.title: Midwinter Closes
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Storms trap the party in a mountain pass; hunters close in. Orsen uses the gift to rally wolves to their defense — a public, undeniable display of magic. Emotional beat: no more hiding; fear transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Taken
chapters.summary: Tammas's POV. He arrests Orsen to protect them from harsher hands, intending to smuggle them free. Instead the crown decides to make an example: Orsen will burn at the solstice. Emotional beat: good intentions becoming catastrophe.

chapters.title: The Cell Below
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. In prison, rats and ravens carry messages between Orsen and Yara outside. Orsen confronts what speaking the covenant might cost and decides, quietly, that a life hidden was never fully lived. Emotional beat: acceptance; identity chosen over survival.

chapters.title: Solstice Fire
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge. At the pyre, Yara and Ilex breach the square with Vessith's ember; Tammas turns his sword on his fellow hunters. Chaos, fire, and the crowd watching magic done openly for the first time in a generation. Emotional beat: climax — everything risked at once.

chapters.title: The Speaking
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. On the pyre's ashes, with Vessith's last flame rising, Orsen speaks the covenant words in the old tongue, voice joined by Yara, Ilex, and — faltering, then certain — Tammas. The fire does not gutter; it blooms. Emotional beat: transcendence through shared voice.

chapters.title: After the Ashes
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The edict collapses; the crown, facing a people who watched the miracle, rescinds the hunt. Dragons begin to wake across the northern ranges. Yara's coven sends word lifting her exile. Emotional beat: exhale; the world remade in small mercies.

chapters.title: Kavanagh, Beast-Speaker
chapters.summary: Tammas's POV. Brothers reconcile imperfectly — no absolution, just a shared meal and an honest accounting. Tammas resigns his commission to become the covenant's first sworn protector. Emotional beat: reconciliation without erasure of harm.

chapters.title: Hearth-Fire and Salt
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, epilogue. A new stall in a rebuilt Greyharbor, charms sold openly beside Yara's salt-work, Vessith's shadow warming the rooftops. Orsen greets the morning by speaking with every creature that passes. Emotional beat: belonging; the gift finally at home.
